title: VPNs and tunnels
summary: Packets inside packets: IPsec, WireGuard, SSH tunnels, split tunnelling and their MTU cost.

steps.title: A packet inside a packet
body: A **tunnel** wraps a whole packet inside another, usually encrypted, so private networks can talk across the internet:
- **Site-to-site**: two offices' routers keep a tunnel up; users don't notice.
- **Remote access**: a laptop connects into the company network.
- **IPsec** (IKE to negotiate keys, ESP to carry data) is the traditional standard; **WireGuard** is small and fast, UDP-only, configured with public keys; **OpenVPN** runs over TLS.

steps.prompt: Match each technology to its description.
pairs: IKE negotiates keys, ESP carries traffic
Public-key peers over UDP, routes by AllowedIPs
Forward one local port through an SSH server
SOCKS proxy through an SSH server

steps.prompt: WireGuard over IPv4 adds 60 bytes of headers. What inner MTU and TCP MSS fit a 1500-byte path?
steps.explain: WireGuard's default of 1420 also leaves room for IPv6 outer headers.

steps.title: Split tunnel, full tunnel
body: - **Full tunnel**: *all* traffic goes through the VPN (`AllowedIPs = 0.0.0.0/0`). The company sees and filters everything; slower for video calls.
- **Split tunnel**: only company ranges go through it (`AllowedIPs = 10.0.0.0/8`); the rest uses the local internet.

WireGuard does **crypto-key routing**: each peer has a list of AllowedIPs, and an outgoing packet goes to the peer whose AllowedIPs match its destination most specifically. Incoming packets are accepted only if their inner source is in the sending peer's AllowedIPs.
SSH tunnels are the pocket-knife version:
ssh -L 5432:db.internal:5432 bastion   # localhost:5432 -> db.internal:5432 via bastion
ssh -D 1080 bastion                    # SOCKS proxy on localhost:1080

steps.prompt: With a split tunnel for `10.0.0.0/8`, where does each go?
Complete the command: make the internal database `db.internal:5432` reachable on your laptop's port 15432 via `bastion`.
steps.explain: `-L local_port:remote_host:remote_port`: the remote host is resolved and reached from the bastion.

steps.prompt: A developer runs `ssh -R 0.0.0.0:8080:localhost:3000 vps` to show a demo. What's the security concern?
options: Anyone on the internet who can reach vps:8080 now reaches the developer's local app (and through it, possibly the office network)
It disables the firewall on the laptop
steps.explain: Tunnels bypass perimeter controls. Remote forwards to 0.0.0.0 are exactly what `GatewayPorts no` exists to stop.

steps.prompt: Users on the VPN can reach internal IPs but `wiki.corp.example` doesn't resolve. Most likely?
options: The VPN doesn't push the internal DNS server (or split DNS for corp.example)
steps.explain: Routing and name resolution are separate: a VPN must provide both.

steps.title: Crypto-key routing
prompt: Write `string Peer(List<(string Name, List<string> AllowedIps)> peers, string dst)` returning the peer whose AllowedIPs contain `dst` with the **longest** prefix,
starter: uint ToUInt(string ip) => ip.Split('.').Aggregate(0u, (acc, o) => (acc << 8) | uint.Parse(o));
uint MaskOf(int prefix) => prefix == 0 ? 0u : uint.MaxValue << (32 - prefix);
string Peer(List<(string Name, List<string> AllowedIps)> peers, string dst)
solution: uint ToUInt(string ip) => ip.Split('.').Aggregate(0u, (acc, o) => (acc << 8) | uint.Parse(o));
uint MaskOf(int prefix) => prefix == 0 ? 0u : uint.MaxValue << (32 - prefix);
string Peer(List<(string Name, List<string> AllowedIps)> peers, string dst)
if ((ToUInt(dst) & MaskOf(len)) == (ToUInt(p[0]) & MaskOf(len)) && len > bestLen) { best = name; bestLen = len; }
template: var dojoP = new List<(string Name, List<string> AllowedIps)> {
Dojo.Eq("second range of a peer", "lab", Peer(dojoP, "192.168.77.20"));
Dojo.Eq("full tunnel peer", "exit", Peer(new List<(string Name, List<string> AllowedIps)> { ("exit", new List<string> { "0.0.0.0/0" }) }, "8.8.8.8"));
hints: Loop over every peer and every CIDR.
Keep the match with the biggest prefix.

steps.title: Parse an SSH forward
prompt: Write `(string Kind, int Listen, string Host, int Port) ParseForward(string arg)`:
An optional bind address may come first: `"-L 127.0.0.1:8080:web:80"` has listen port 8080. Anything else throws `FormatException`.
starter: (string Kind, int Listen, string Host, int Port) ParseForward(string arg)
solution: (string Kind, int Listen, string Host, int Port) ParseForward(string arg)
if (parts.Length != 2) throw new FormatException("expected a flag and a spec");
hints: Split the flag from the spec, then split the spec on `:`.
Count from the end (`f[^1]`, `f[^2]`, `f[^3]`) so an optional bind address doesn't matter.
